children: was upgraded to Buy from Neutral with a $38 price target at Guggenheim following the nuclear technology company's
, which showed progress on key milestones toward commercial operations.
But shares fell 2.9% in Friday's trading and have plunged 25% in two weeks, as the nuclear sector has been dragged down in the current AI selloff.
Guggenheim analyst Joseph Osha said he came away from the Q3 update encouraged by Oklo's

continued execution against key milestones building towards commercial operations across the power, isotopes, and fuel businesses, but the stock has plunged 80% from its January 9 peak compared to a 3% increase for the S&P 500 during the period.

Osha pointed to "the velocity with which Oklo management continues to demonstrate commercial progress on schedule," and said the company has not received enough credit for the accelerated completion of Groves-1, since the project was completed entirely on its own and well ahead of schedule; because of that success, another reactor is now already underway and targeting first commercial isotope delivery as soon as next year.

"It is now more clear to us that Oklo's deliberate focus on de-risking key items and processes across the business ahead of time is beginning to pay off, as the focus shifts from development to deployment across power, isotopes, and fuel," Osha wrote.
The analyst also noted the Groves-1 reactor recently entered an R&D phase granted by the Department of Energy and will begin testing isotope capabilities, providing Oklo
with "a somewhat unanticipated head start on commercial product development for Groves-2," and INL, the gating item, has broken ground, with the site moving to vertical construction.

title: Oklo raised to Buy at Guggenheim on execution progress but shares extend slide
